choices.text: A compound that contains chirality centers but is achiral overall
A 50 : 50 mixture of two enantiomers
choices.why: That is a racemic mixture. A meso compound is a single compound whose molecules are themselves achiral.

choices.text: A chiral compound with more than one chirality center
choices.why: A meso compound is achiral, despite having chirality centers, because it has a plane of symmetry.

choices.text: A compound with no chirality centers
choices.why: Such a compound is simply achiral. What makes a meso compound special is that it has chirality centers and is still achiral.

explanation: Compounds that are achiral, yet contain chirality centers, are called meso compounds. meso-Tartaric acid has two chirality centers but also a plane of symmetry, so it is achiral.

prompt: Tartaric acid, HO2CCH(OH)CH(OH)CO2H, has two chirality centers. How many stereoisomers of tartaric acid actually exist?
explanation: Four structures can be drawn (2R,3R; 2S,3S; 2R,3S; 2S,3R), but 2R,3S and 2S,3R are identical because the molecule has a plane of symmetry. Tartaric acid therefore exists in three stereoisomeric forms: two enantiomers and one meso form.

prompt: Four configurations can be drawn for tartaric acid, HO2CCH(OH)CH(OH)CO2H: 2R,3R; 2S,3S; 2R,3S; and 2S,3R. Which two turn out to be the same compound?

choices.text: 2R,3S and 2S,3R
2R,3R and 2S,3S
choices.why: These are nonsuperimposable mirror images, so they are a pair of enantiomers, not the same compound.

choices.text: 2R,3R and 2R,3S
choices.why: These differ at only one of the two chirality centers and are not mirror images; they are different stereoisomers (diastereomers).

choices.text: None; all four are different stereoisomers
choices.why: Two chirality centers allow at most four stereoisomers, but here two of the structures are superimposable, so there are only three.

explanation: A close look at the 2R,3S and 2S,3R structures shows that they are superimposable, and thus identical, as can be seen by rotating one structure 180°. The molecule has a plane of symmetry and is achiral: it is meso-tartaric acid.

prompt: Where is the plane of symmetry in meso-tartaric acid, HO2CCH(OH)CH(OH)CO2H?

choices.text: It cuts through the C2–C3 bond, making one half of the molecule a mirror image of the other half
It passes through C2, containing the C2–OH bond
choices.why: A plane through only one chirality center would not relate the two halves of the molecule. The plane lies between C2 and C3.

choices.text: It contains all four carbon atoms
choices.why: The plane relates the C2 half of the molecule to the C3 half, so it cuts across the C2–C3 bond rather than containing the carbon chain.

choices.text: There is none; meso-tartaric acid is achiral because it has no chirality centers
choices.why: C2 and C3 are both chirality centers. The molecule is achiral because of its symmetry plane.

explanation: The symmetry plane cuts through the C2–C3 bond, making one half of the molecule a mirror image of the other half (Figure 5.7.1). Because of this plane, the molecule is achiral despite having two chirality centers.

prompt: How many chirality centers does meso-tartaric acid, HO2CCH(OH)CH(OH)CO2H, have?
explanation: C2 and C3 are both chirality centers, each bonded to H, OH, CO2H and the rest of the molecule. meso-Tartaric acid is achiral anyway, because a plane of symmetry through the C2–C3 bond makes one half the mirror image of the other.

prompt: What is the relationship between (2R,3R)-tartaric acid and (2S,3S)-tartaric acid?

choices.text: They are enantiomers
They are identical, like the 2R,3S and 2S,3R structures
choices.why: Only 2R,3S and 2S,3R are superimposable, because that form has a symmetry plane. The 2R,3R and 2S,3S forms are nonsuperimposable mirror images.

choices.text: They are diastereomers
choices.why: Diastereomers are stereoisomers that are not mirror images. 2R,3R and 2S,3S are opposite at both centers, so they are mirror images.

choices.text: They are both meso compounds
choices.why: Each is chiral and optically active: they are (+)- and (−)-tartaric acid, with [α]D = +12 and −12.

explanation: The 2R,3R and 2S,3S structures are nonsuperimposable mirror images and therefore represent a pair of enantiomers, the (+)- and (−)-tartaric acids of Table 5.7.1.

prompt: What is the relationship between meso-tartaric acid and (+)-tartaric acid?

choices.text: They are diastereomers
They are enantiomers
choices.why: meso-Tartaric acid has no mirror-image relationship to the (+) and (−) forms; its mirror image is itself.

choices.text: They are the same compound, because both contain two chirality centers
choices.why: Having the same number of chirality centers doesn't make two compounds identical. The meso form differs in configuration and has different physical properties.

choices.text: They are not stereoisomers, because one is chiral and the other is achiral
choices.why: They have the same atoms connected in the same order and differ only in the three-dimensional arrangement at C2 and C3, so they are stereoisomers.

explanation: The meso isomer is diastereomeric with the (+) and (−) forms. It has no mirror-image relationship to (+)- and (−)-tartaric acids, is a different compound altogether, and thus has different physical properties (Table 5.7.1).

prompt: Why does a pure sample of meso-tartaric acid show no optical rotation?

choices.text: Each molecule is achiral, because it has a plane of symmetry
It is a 50 : 50 mixture of the 2R,3S and 2S,3R molecules, whose rotations cancel
choices.why: 2R,3S and 2S,3R are not two different molecules; they are superimposable, and thus identical. The cancellation idea describes a racemic mixture.

choices.text: It has no chirality centers
choices.why: C2 and C3 are both chirality centers. The molecule is achiral despite them, because of its symmetry plane.

choices.text: Both of its chirality centers have the R configuration
choices.why: The meso form is 2R,3S (the same as 2S,3R). The 2R,3R form is (+)-tartaric acid, which is optically active.

explanation: The 2R,3S structure has a plane of symmetry through the C2–C3 bond, so the molecule is achiral despite its two chirality centers. Table 5.7.1 gives meso-tartaric acid an [α]D of 0.

prompt: According to Table 5.7.1, what is the specific rotation [α]D of meso-tartaric acid?
explanation: meso-Tartaric acid is achiral because of its plane of symmetry, so it does not rotate plane-polarized light: Table 5.7.1 lists its [α]D as 0, compared with +12 and −12 for the two enantiomers.

prompt: (+)-Tartaric acid has [α]D = +12. What is the specific rotation [α]D of (−)-tartaric acid?
explanation: (+)- and (−)-tartaric acids are enantiomers. They have identical melting points, solubilities and densities, but they differ in the sign of their rotation of plane-polarized light: Table 5.7.1 gives +12 and −12.

prompt: According to Table 5.7.1, which property differs between (+)-tartaric acid and (−)-tartaric acid?

choices.text: The sign of the specific rotation
The melting point
choices.why: Both enantiomers melt at 168–170 °C. Only the meso form, a diastereomer, melts differently (146–148 °C).

choices.text: The solubility in water
choices.why: Both enantiomers dissolve to 139.0 g/100 mL H2O at 20 °C.

choices.text: The density
choices.why: Both enantiomers have a density of 1.7598 g/cm^3.

explanation: The (+)- and (−)-tartaric acids have identical melting points, solubilities, and densities, but they differ in the sign of their rotation of plane-polarized light ([α]D = +12 and −12, Table 5.7.1).

prompt: (+)- and (−)-tartaric acid both melt at 168–170 °C, but meso-tartaric acid melts at 146–148 °C. Why is the meso form different?

choices.text: It is a diastereomer of the other two, a different compound altogether, so it has different physical properties
It is a mixture of two forms, which lowers its melting point
choices.why: meso-Tartaric acid is a single compound; its 2R,3S and 2S,3R structures are identical.

choices.text: Its lack of optical rotation lowers its melting point
choices.why: Optical rotation doesn't cause the difference. The meso form differs in many properties because it is a diastereomer.

choices.text: It has fewer chirality centers than the (+) and (−) forms
choices.why: All three stereoisomers have two chirality centers, at C2 and C3.

explanation: The meso isomer is diastereomeric with the (+) and (−) forms. It has no mirror-image relationship to them, is a different compound altogether, and thus has different physical properties: lower melting point, density and solubility (Table 5.7.1).

prompt: Using Table 5.7.1, how much more soluble in water at 20 °C is (+)-tartaric acid than meso-tartaric acid, in g/100 mL H2O?
explanation: Table 5.7.1 gives solubilities of 139.0 g/100 mL H2O for (+)-tartaric acid and 125.0 g/100 mL for the meso form: 139.0 − 125.0 = 14.0 g/100 mL. The meso form is a diastereomer, so its physical properties differ.

prompt: 2,3-Dibromobutane, CH3CHBrCHBrCH3, has two chirality centers, and its 2R,3S form has a plane of symmetry. How many stereoisomers of 2,3-dibromobutane exist?
explanation: Like tartaric acid, the two halves of the molecule are identical. The 2R,3R and 2S,3S forms are a pair of enantiomers, while 2R,3S and 2S,3R are superimposable, the same achiral meso compound. That gives three stereoisomers rather than four.

choices.text: C1 and C2 are chirality centers, but the molecule is achiral: it is a meso compound
It is chiral, because it has two chirality centers
choices.why: Not all molecules with chirality centers are chiral overall. The cis isomer has a symmetry plane bisecting the ring between C1 and C2.

choices.text: It has no chirality centers, because C1 and C2 are bonded to identical groups
choices.why: Each of C1 and C2 is bonded to H, Br, the other bromine-bearing carbon, and a CH2 of the ring: four different groups.

choices.text: It has one chirality center, because C1 and C2 are equivalent
choices.why: Being related by symmetry doesn't merge two atoms into one. C1 and C2 are each a chirality center.

explanation: Look for carbons bonded to four different groups to find chirality centers, and look for a symmetry plane to decide whether the molecule is chiral. Both bromine-bearing carbons are chirality centers, but a symmetry plane bisects the ring between C1 and C2 in the cis isomer, so it is a meso compound (compare Worked Example 5.7.1).

prompt: Which of these compounds has a meso form?

choices.text: 3,4-Dimethylhexane, CH3CH2CH(CH3)CH(CH3)CH2CH3
3,4-Dimethylheptane, CH3CH2CH(CH3)CH(CH3)CH2CH2CH3
choices.why: It has two chirality centers, but one carries an ethyl group and the other a propyl group. The two halves differ, so no stereoisomer can have a symmetry plane.

choices.text: 2-Chlorobutane, CH3CHClCH2CH3
choices.why: With only one chirality center, the molecule is always chiral; a meso compound needs at least two chirality centers.

choices.text: 2,3-Dimethylpentane, (CH3)2CHCH(CH3)CH2CH3
choices.why: C2 carries two methyl groups, so it isn't a chirality center. The molecule has only one chirality center (C3) and cannot be meso.

explanation: A meso compound has chirality centers yet is achiral because of a plane of symmetry. In 3,4-dimethylhexane, C3 and C4 are chirality centers with identical sets of groups, so the 3R,4S form has a symmetry plane through the C3–C4 bond, just like meso-tartaric acid.

prompt: A molecule has two chirality centers. How do you decide whether it is chiral?

choices.text: Look for a plane of symmetry: if it has one, it is achiral
No test is needed; any molecule with chirality centers is chiral
choices.why: Meso compounds are the exception: they have chirality centers but are achiral.

choices.text: Assign R or S to each center; it is chiral only if both centers are R or both are S
choices.why: R,R versus R,S doesn't decide chirality in general. meso-Tartaric acid is 2R,3S because its two halves are mirror images, but a molecule with different halves is chiral whatever its labels.

choices.text: Count the chirality centers: an even number makes the molecule achiral
choices.why: (+)-Tartaric acid has two chirality centers and is chiral. Only a symmetry plane makes the molecule achiral.

explanation: To see whether a chirality center is present, look for a carbon atom bonded to four different groups. To see whether the molecule is chiral, look for the presence or absence of a symmetry plane. Not all molecules with chirality centers are chiral overall—meso compounds are an exception.
